findings.rationale: Both records have the same supplier (Northstar Office), invoice number (NS-204), date (2026-10-03) and amount (184500 cents). The records match on every field. No payment evidence was purchased for this pair, so whether both were paid is unverified.

The invoices share a supplier and amount (72500 cents), and the invoice numbers differ (AC-902 vs AC-902-R, dated one day apart), which suggests a reissue. Purchased evidence PAY-B shows payment P-B1 was reversed in full before replacement payment P-B2 settled, so the net result is one settled payment. The reversal should be confirmed by a reviewer against bank records.

The invoices have the same amount (96000 cents) and near-identical supplier names and invoice numbers (Meridian Labs Ltd ML-431 vs Meridian Laboratory M-431, one day apart). Purchased evidence PAY-C shows two settled payments to the same bank account, each citing PO-431 and delivery note DN-431. Both payments settled, so this is a likely duplicate payment, pending reviewer confirmation of the vendor identity.

Both records are from Harbor Storage for the same amount (30000 cents), but they have different dates (2026-09-01 and 2026-10-01), and the invoice reference 'MONTHLY' indicates recurring monthly billing. This pattern is consistent with a legitimate recurring charge. No payment evidence was purchased.

caveat: Four synthetic pairs; baseline latency measures local computation only, while agent latency includes network and model time. Expenditure excludes model provider costs.
